title: Chip Industry Week In Review
gist: Weekly chip-industry roundup dominated by HBM and memory scarcity (sold out through 2029 at SK hynix), rising CoWoS packaging prices, record AI-driven earnings across memory, test and packaging, and agentic AI entering chip design.

insights.claim: SK hynix expects memory supply constraints to persist through 2030, with DRAM and HBM volumes effectively sold out through 2029.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Multi-year visibility supports memory pricing power and capex-driven beneficiaries.

insights.claim: Samsung expects tight memory supply through 2028 and says its 2027 HBM supply is already sold out, citing long fab construction and equipment lead times, larger dies, more complex next-gen HBM processes, and DRAM capacity shifting toward HBM.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Supply is structurally constrained, not just cyclical; watch conventional DRAM tightness from capacity diversion to HBM.

insights.claim: Anthropic warned in its IPO filing that HBM shortages and limited TSMC manufacturing capacity could constrain AI expansion.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Even leading AI labs name memory and foundry capacity as binding constraints on growth.

insights.claim: China's CXMT plans limited HBM3E production soon despite yields of only 20% to 30%, per Reuters.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Chinese HBM entry is real but low-yield; limited near-term threat to incumbents' supply tightness.

insights.claim: Solidigm, SK hynix's U.S. subsidiary, is reportedly discussing a proposed $45B NAND flash fab with the U.S. Commerce Department.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Signals potential large U.S. NAND onshoring supported by government; unconfirmed.

insights.claim: TSMC is reportedly considering a 20% price increase for CoWoS as AI demand strains advanced-packaging capacity.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Packaging pricing power flows to TSMC margins and raises AI accelerator costs.

insights.claim: ASE forecasts its advanced-packaging revenue will double in 2027, and Amkor is ramping new high-density fan-out and 2.5D packaging programs.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: OSAT players are capturing spillover advanced-packaging demand.

insights.claim: Applied Materials plans to raise its stake in Besi to about 20%, deepening a partnership extending from hybrid bonding into new interconnect architectures for AI packaging.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Hybrid bonding equipment is strategic enough for toolmakers to take equity stakes; watch for further consolidation.

insights.claim: UMC approved an extra $3.2B of capital spending for Singapore and Tainan expansion as demand grows for advanced packaging and silicon photonics, with fab utilization reaching 92%.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Mature-node foundries are benefiting from packaging and photonics demand with high utilization.

insights.claim: Intel Foundry reported better yields and cycle times on 18A in Q3, released the 14A 0.9 PDK in October, and continues talks with prospective external customers for 18A-P and 14A.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Execution improvement is a precondition for external foundry wins; watch for named customers.

insights.claim: Infineon plans to invest EUR 1.1B through 2034 at Villach, Austria for Europe's first high-volume next-gen GaN power semiconductor facility on 300mm wafers.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: 300mm GaN scaling targets AI data center power cost reduction.

insights.claim: Vietnam's first semiconductor fab, the roughly US$1.3B Viettel project, may miss its 2027 trial-production target, with construction not begun and ASML lithography negotiations unresolved, per Reuters; Viettel says it is on schedule.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Emerging-market fab ambitions face execution and equipment-access risk.

themes.theme: AI compute and custom silicon demand

insights.claim: OpenAI is reportedly planning to buy Google TPUs, and Oracle will offer Google TPUs through its cloud from 2027 and add Arm AGI CPUs in fall 2027.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Non-Nvidia accelerators are gaining third-party distribution, a diversification signal for AI buyers.

insights.claim: Broadcom XPUs and networking gear will support Anthropic's AI infrastructure expansion from 2027 under a $63B financing arrangement.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Large financed custom-silicon commitments lock in Broadcom's multi-year AI revenue.

insights.claim: Meta is expanding Nvidia and AMD AI infrastructure across its data centers, with both chipmakers also taking stakes in Meta.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Vendor equity stakes in customers show circular financing in AI buildouts.

insights.claim: SK hynix posted record revenue of KRW 104.6T, up 328% year over year, and Samsung KRW 195.3T, up 127%, with a major HBM4 ramp.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Memory makers are seeing extreme growth; the earnings trajectory reflects the scarcity narrative.

insights.claim: Test and packaging suppliers show strong AI-driven growth: Advantest revenue up 82%, Teradyne up 70% with record memory and systems test revenue, ASE up 45%, and Amkor net income up 50% on richer advanced-packaging mix.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Picks-and-shovels in test and packaging are growing faster than many chip designers.

insights.claim: Intel revenue was $16.5B, up 21%, with 78% from data center and AI and foundry revenue up 58%; Cadence revenue was $1.6B, up 22%, with record backlog of $8.2B.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Cadence's backlog gives EDA revenue visibility; Intel mix is shifting toward data center and foundry.

themes.theme: Agentic AI in chip design and CPUs

insights.claim: Cadence introduced domain-specialized AI models for agentic chip and system design, combining post-trained LLMs, decision models, and self-improving agent skills integrated with its EDA tools.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: EDA vendors are embedding agentic AI to defend and extend tool franchises.

insights.claim: Arm introduced a CPU benchmarking methodology for agentic AI workloads covering tool execution, orchestration, and reasoning, using repeatable measurements and end-to-end task outcomes.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Defining the benchmark for agentic workloads lets Arm frame CPU relevance in AI.

insights.claim: Intel plans to acquire Classiq to add automated quantum algorithm synthesis software to its silicon spin-qubit technology and manufacturing for a full-stack quantum offering.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Intel is pursuing a vertically integrated quantum position.

insights.claim: Reported but unconfirmed deals include Marvell in advanced talks to acquire Lumentum, and onsemi in talks to buy Ferric for nearly $1B; FuriosaAI raised $620M.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Optical and power-delivery assets are acquisition targets as AI scales; treat as rumor.

insights.claim: TianoCore disclosed a critical EDK II UEFI flaw enabling unauthenticated network code execution during PXE boot, before Secure Boot or measured boot can verify anything, and Supermicro disclosed nine BMC firmware vulnerabilities including a critical unauthenticated IPMI flaw.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Firmware-layer vulnerabilities in server infrastructure raise hardware security spending relevance.
